questionText: Six people are seated around a circular table. There are at least two men and two women. There are at least three right-handed persons. Every woman has a left-handed person to her immediate right. None of the women are right-handed. The number of women at the table is
explanation:
Step 1: Analyze the given constraints.
• Total people seated = $6$.
• There are at least $2$ men ($M \ge 2$) and at least $2$ women ($W \ge 2$).
• There are at least $3$ right-handed persons.
• None of the women are right-handed, which means all women are left-handed.
• Since no women are right-handed, all right-handed persons must be men. Therefore, there are at least $3$ right-handed men ($M \ge 3$).

Step 2: Evaluate possible combinations for the number of men ($M$) and women ($W$).
Since $M + W = 6$, $M \ge 3$, and $W \ge 2$, the possible cases are:
1. $M = 3, W = 3$
2. $M = 4, W = 2$

Step 3: Test Case 1 ($W = 3, M = 3$).
If $M = 3$, all $3$ men must be right-handed to satisfy the condition of at least $3$ right-handed persons.
This leaves only the $3$ women as left-handed persons.
The problem specifies that every woman has a left-handed person to her immediate right.
If only women are left-handed, then every woman must have another woman to her immediate right. On a circular table, this implies that every woman is immediately followed by a woman, which would force all $6$ seats to be occupied by women. This contradicts $M = 3$. Hence, $W = 3$ is impossible.

Step 4: Test Case 2 ($W = 2, M = 4$).
If $W = 2$ and $M = 4$, among the $4$ men, $3$ can be right-handed and $1$ can be left-handed.
This gives $3$ left-handed persons ($2$ women + $1$ man).
We can arrange them in circular order as: $W_2 \rightarrow W_1 \rightarrow M_{\text{left}} \rightarrow M_{\text{right1}} \rightarrow M_{\text{right2}} \rightarrow M_{\text{right3}} \rightarrow W_2$.
• $W_2$'s immediate right is $W_1$ (left-handed).
• $W_1$'s immediate right is $M_{\text{left}}$ (left-handed).
All conditions are satisfied.

Therefore, the number of women at the table is 2.
